# cloudxino_reserved_ip_assignment (Resource)

Points a `cloudxino_reserved_ip` at a CC2 server or a CC2 load balancer (exactly one of `server_id`, `load_balancer_id`). Kept apart from the reserved IP so the address stays the team's when the target is replaced: the assignment moves to the new one. Destroying it unassigns the address (the reserved IP itself stays). A CKS LoadBalancer Service asks for a reserved IP with its own annotation `cloudxino.com/reserved-ip: <address>` instead.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Keep the address when the server is replaced: the reserved IP has no server_id, and the
# assignment moves to the new server.
resource "cloudxino_reserved_ip" "web" {
  region = "dhaka-1" # the server must be in this region
}

resource "cloudxino_reserved_ip_assignment" "web" {
  reserved_ip_id = cloudxino_reserved_ip.web.id
  server_id      = cloudxino_server.web.id
}

# Or point it at a CC2 load balancer (exactly one of server_id, load_balancer_id).
resource "cloudxino_reserved_ip_assignment" "lb" {
  reserved_ip_id   = cloudxino_reserved_ip.lb.id
  load_balancer_id = cloudxino_load_balancer.web.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `reserved_ip_id` (String) ID of the `cloudxino_reserved_ip`.

### Optional

- `load_balancer_id` (String) ID of a `cloudxino_load_balancer` in the reserved IP's region: its forwarding rules answer on the reserved address too. Changing it moves the address without a gap.
- `server_id` (String) ID of a `cloudxino_server` in the reserved IP's region. Changing it moves the address without a gap.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The reserved IP's ID.
- `ip_address` (String) The reserved address.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# the ID is the reserved IP's ID
terraform import cloudxino_reserved_ip_assignment.web <reserved_ip_id>
```
